coachingInstructions.missedSession: Skip or move one session only if the next key session and recovery still fit. Do not stack missed quality, heavy work or long runs. After two missed sessions, illness or a week away, review the next block.
coachingInstructions.liftingEffort: Warm up to the prescribed effort. RPE governs the suggested kg. If effort overshoots by a point, reduce 2.5–5% and reassess; if still excessive, omit remaining back-offs. Heavy singles are skill practice, not forced maximal attempts.
coachingInstructions.speedWork: Accelerate with stable technique. Reduce load or stop when speed or position deteriorates. An easy speed day is not permission to turn it into a heavy day.
coachingInstructions.athleteJudgement: Report sustained fatigue, sleep disruption, pain, illness or altered movement. End the provoking work when needed. One difficult session is a reason to adjust that session, not an automatic full deload.
coachingInstructions.review: Review completed work every four weeks and after events. Later blocks are conditional on observed recovery and performance; no race result or lifting total is guaranteed.

Strength exposure: demanding main work followed by a smaller volume dose. RPE 8 governs the load: warm up, adjust the suggestion to the day, and log actual effort. If the first work set is at least one RPE above target, lower subsequent load 2.5–5%; if effort remains high, omit the last back-off and report the overshoot. No failed reps or extra max attempts.

Lat pulldown (8–10 reps): Vertical pulling and upper-back support. Keep this movement through the block; work within 8–10 reps at the target RPE. Choose the first working load by RPE; no load is borrowed from bench or another variation.

Triceps pushdown (10–12 reps): Triceps support without another heavy press. Keep this movement through the block; work within 10–12 reps at the target RPE. Choose the first working load by RPE; no load is borrowed from bench or another variation.

Reverse pec deck (12–15 reps): Rear-delt development. Keep this movement through the block; work within 12–15 reps at the target RPE. Choose the first working load by RPE; no load is borrowed from bench or another variation.

coachingInstructions.missedSession: Skip or move one session only if the next key session and recovery still fit. Do not stack missed quality, heavy work or long runs. After two missed sessions, illness or a week away, review the next block.
coachingInstructions.liftingEffort: Warm up to the prescribed effort. RPE governs the suggested kg. If effort overshoots by a point, reduce 2.5–5% and reassess; if still excessive, omit remaining back-offs. Heavy singles are skill practice, not forced maximal attempts.
coachingInstructions.speedWork: Accelerate with stable technique. Reduce load or stop when speed or position deteriorates. An easy speed day is not permission to turn it into a heavy day.
coachingInstructions.athleteJudgement: Report sustained fatigue, sleep disruption, pain, illness or altered movement. End the provoking work when needed. One difficult session is a reason to adjust that session, not an automatic full deload.
coachingInstructions.review: Review completed work every four weeks and after events. Later blocks are conditional on observed recovery and performance; no race result or lifting total is guaranteed.

coachingInstructions.liftingEffort: Warm up to the prescribed effort. RPE governs the suggested kg. If effort overshoots by a point, reduce 2.5–5% and reassess; if still excessive, omit remaining back-offs. Heavy singles are skill practice, not forced maximal attempts.

variationNotes: Heavy competition single; practise setup, pause and commands. RPE 8 governs the load: warm up, adjust the suggestion to the day, and log actual effort. If the first work set is at least one RPE above target, lower subsequent load 2.5–5%; if effort remains high, omit the last back-off and report the overshoot. No failed reps or extra max attempts.
Hip thrust (10–12 reps): Block 2: Hip extension strength. Choose initial load by RPE; aim to add reps before weight.
Seated cable row (10–12 reps): Block 2: Upper-back strength. Choose initial load by RPE; aim to add reps before weight.

Speed / technique: competition setup and commands, then accelerate every double. Use 60–90 seconds between sets; extend rest if needed for quality. Load is a starting suggestion, not a speed test. Stop the set or reduce load when speed or position deteriorates; no grinders.

Machine shoulder press (8–10 reps): Controlled shoulder pressing. Keep this movement through the block; work within 8–10 reps at the target RPE. Choose the first working load by RPE; no load is borrowed from bench or another variation.

Chest-supported cable row (10–12 reps): Horizontal pulling with a different setup. Keep this movement through the block; work within 10–12 reps at the target RPE. Choose the first working load by RPE; no load is borrowed from bench or another variation.

Cable rear-delt fly (12–15 reps): Rear-shoulder and scapular control. Keep this movement through the block; work within 12–15 reps at the target RPE. Choose the first working load by RPE; no load is borrowed from bench or another variation.

coachingInstructions.missedSession: Skip or move one session only if the next key session and recovery still fit. Do not stack missed quality, heavy work or long runs. After two missed sessions, illness or a week away, review the next block.
coachingInstructions.liftingEffort: Warm up to the prescribed effort. RPE governs the suggested kg. If effort overshoots by a point, reduce 2.5–5% and reassess; if still excessive, omit remaining back-offs. Heavy singles are skill practice, not forced maximal attempts.
coachingInstructions.speedWork: Accelerate with stable technique. Reduce load or stop when speed or position deteriorates. An easy speed day is not permission to turn it into a heavy day.
coachingInstructions.athleteJudgement: Report sustained fatigue, sleep disruption, pain, illness or altered movement. End the provoking work when needed. One difficult session is a reason to adjust that session, not an automatic full deload.
coachingInstructions.review: Review completed work every four weeks and after events. Later blocks are conditional on observed recovery and performance; no race result or lifting total is guaranteed.

warnings: Maintain an easy aerobic base for the later marathon while strength has priority. Race-specific running starts after the dated handover and recovery review.
Confirm recent long-run distance and recovery before extending the endurance-support long run; a past marathon does not establish present long-run readiness.
fuelling: Practise carbohydrate and fluid intake during long runs, rather than introducing it on race day. Start with familiar small portions totalling about 30 g carbohydrate/hour; progress towards 45–60 g/hour on longer rehearsals if tolerated.
Drink to conditions and thirst; record what you actually tolerate. Use the same foods/drinks in later race rehearsals.

coachingInstructions.missedSession: Skip or move one session only if the next key session and recovery still fit. Do not stack missed quality, heavy work or long runs. After two missed sessions, illness or a week away, review the next block.
coachingInstructions.liftingEffort: Warm up to the prescribed effort. RPE governs the suggested kg. If effort overshoots by a point, reduce 2.5–5% and reassess; if still excessive, omit remaining back-offs. Heavy singles are skill practice, not forced maximal attempts.
coachingInstructions.speedWork: Accelerate with stable technique. Reduce load or stop when speed or position deteriorates. An easy speed day is not permission to turn it into a heavy day.
coachingInstructions.athleteJudgement: Report sustained fatigue, sleep disruption, pain, illness or altered movement. End the provoking work when needed. One difficult session is a reason to adjust that session, not an automatic full deload.
coachingInstructions.review: Review completed work every four weeks and after events. Later blocks are conditional on observed recovery and performance; no race result or lifting total is guaranteed.
